Could use vectorization.\n\nWe\'ll implement with for_loop(par) for j and i.\n\nEdge cases: N==0.\n\nProvide example usage.\n\nLet\'s craft final answer with code snippet.\n\nassistantfinal**Solution Overview**\n\nWe implement the classic Doolittle LU‑decomposition (no pivoting) **in‑place** on a\nrow‑major `std::vector<double>` that stores an `N × N` matrix `A`.  \nAfter the routine finishes the lower‑triangular part (including the diagonal)\ncontains the `L` matrix (with an implicit unit diagonal) and the upper‑triangular\npart contains the `U` matrix.\n\nThe algorithm is\n\n```\nfor k = 0 … N‑1\n    // ---------- compute the k‑th row of U ----------\n    for j = k … N‑1\n        A[k,j] ← A[k,j] – Σ_{p=0}^{k‑1} L[k,p]·U[p,j]\n\n    // ---------- compute the k‑th column of L ----------\n    for i = k+1 … N‑1\n        A[i,k] ← ( A[i,k] – Σ_{p=0}^{k‑1} L[i,p]·U[p,k] ) / A[k,k]\n```\n\nAll work that belongs to a single `k` can be performed **independently** for the\ndifferent `j` (row of `U`) and for the different `i` (column of `L`).  \nTherefore we parallelise those two inner loops with HPX’s `for_loop` using the\n`par` execution policy.  The inner‑most summation over `p` is tiny (at most `k`\niterations) and is left sequential – it is the part that carries the data\ndependencies and cannot be parallelised safely without extra synchronisation.\n\nThe routine does **not** allocate any auxiliary containers, it works directly on\nthe supplied vector, and it returns nothing (the result is stored back into\n`A`).  The code is completely self‑contained and can be compiled with any HPX\ninstallation that provides the `hpx::parallel` algorithms.\n\n---\n\n### Complete, ready‑to‑compile code\n\n```cpp\n//    // 1) Compute the k‑th row of U (columns k … N‑1)\n        // --------------------------------------------------------------\n        for_loop(par, k, N,\n            [&](std::size_t j)\n            {\n                double sum = 0.0;\n                // Σ_{p=0}^{k‑1} L[k,p]·U[p,j]\n                for (std::size_t p = 0; p < k; ++p)\n                {\n                    sum += A[row_k + p] * Overview**\n\nWe implement a classic **Doolittle LU‑factorisation** (unit diagonal in **L**) for a square sparse matrix that is supplied in **COO** format.  \nThe algorithm works on a **dense** `N×N` matrix that is built once from the COO list – this is the cheapest way to obtain good parallel speed‑up because the inner updates touch whole rows/columns and can be performed independently.\n\nThe parallelism is introduced with **HPX**:\n\n* The outer loop over the pivot index `k` stays sequential – each step depends on the previous one.\n* For a given pivot we can update **all rows `i > k` independently**.  \n  HPX’s `hpx::parallel::for_loop` with the `par` execution policy launches a set of lightweight HPX threads that work on disjoint rows, so there are no data races.\n* Inside each row we perform the usual rank‑1 update of the trailing sub‑matrix.\n\nThe public interface matches the prototype you gave:\n\n```cpp\nvoid luFactorize(std::vector<COOElement> const& A,\n                 std::vector<double> &L,\n                 std::vector<double> &U,\n                 size_t N);\n```\n\n`L` and `U` are returned as **dense row‑major vectors** of length `N*N`.  \nIf you need them back in COO format you can trivially post‑process the dense vectors (outside of this routine).\n\n---\n\n### Complete HPX‑enabled implementation\n\n```cpp\n/*  lu_factor_hpx.cpp\n *\n *  Parallel Doolittle LU factorisation for a sparse matrix stored in COO format.\n *  The result is returned as dense row‑major matrices L and U (size N*N).\n *\n *  Compile (example):\n *      g++ -O3 -std=c++20 lu_factor_hpx.cpp -I${HPX_ROOT}/include \\\n *          -L${HPX_ROOT}/lib -lhpx -pthread -o lu_factor_hpx\n *\n *  Run:\n *      ./lu_factor_hpx   // HPX is already initialised by hpx_main.hpp\n */\n\n#include <hpx/hpx_main.hpp>                     // pulls in HPX runtime\n#include <hpx/parallel/algorithms/for_loop.hpp> // hpx::parallel::for_loop\n#include <hpx/execution.hpp>                    // execution policies\n#include <vector>\n#include <cstddef>   // size_t\n#include <stdexcept> // std::runtime_error\n\nstruct COOElement {\n    size_t row, column;\n    double value;\n};\n\n/*  LU factorisation ---------------------------------------------------------\n *\n *  Input:\n *      - A : vector of non‑zero entries in COO format (row‑major indexing)\n *      - N : dimension of the square matrix (A is N×N)\n *\n *  Output (dense, row‑major):\n *      - L : lower triangular matrix with unit diagonal (size N*N)\n *      - U : upper triangular matrix (size N*N)\n *\n *  The routine assumes that the matrix is nonsingular and that all pivots\n *  are non‑zero.  If a zero pivot is encountered a std::runtime_error is\n *  thrown.\n *\n *  Parallelism:\n *      - The outer pivot loop (k) is sequential – each step depends on the\n *        previous one.\n *      - For a fixed pivot, the updates of rows i>k are completely\n *        independent and are executed with hpx::parallel::for_loop using the\n *        `par` execution policy.\n *      - No auxiliary helper functions are used – everything lives inside the\n *        single function body as requested.\n * -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */\nvoid luFactorize(std::vector<COOElement> const& A,\n                 std::vector<double> &L,\n                 std::vector<double> &U,\n                 size_t N)\n{\n    /* ----------------------------------------------------------------------\n     *  1. Allocate dense storage and copy the COO matrix into U.\n     * ---------------------------------------------------------------------- */\n    const size_t NN = N * N;\n    L.assign(NN, 0.0);\n    U.assign(NN, 0.0);\n\n    for (auto const& e : A) {\n        if (e.row >= N || e.column >= N)\n            throw std::runtime_error("COO element out of bounds");\n        U[e.row * N + e.column] = e.value;\n    }\n\n    /* ----------------------------------------------------------------------\n     *  2. Doolittle algorithm – unit diagonal in L.\n     * ---------------------------------------------------------------------- */\n    for (size_t k = 0; k < N; ++k) {\n        // ---- diagonal of L is 1 ------------------------------------------------\n        L[k * N + k] = 1.0;\n\n        // ---- pivot element ----------------------------------------------------\n        double pivot = U[k * N + k];\n        if (pivot == 0.0)\n            throw std::runtime_error("Zero pivot encountered – matrix is singular");\n\n        // ---- compute the k‑th row of U (elements j >= k) -----------------------\n        // (they are already stored in U, we only need them later)\n\n        // ---- update rows i = k+1 … N-1 in parallel ----------------------------\n        hpx::parallel::for_loop(\n            hpx::parallel::execution::par,               // parallel execution policy\n            k + 1, N,\n            [&](size_t i) {\n                // multiplier for the current row\n                double l_ik = U[i * N + k] / pivot;\n                L[i * N + k] = l_ik;\n\n                // rank‑1 update of the trailing sub‑matrix (i, j) for j > k\n
